content: 1. Vedolizumab is indicated for adults with moderate-to-severe active ulcerative colitis and moderate-to-severe active Crohn's disease. 2. Prior to initiating treatment with vedolizumab, all patients should be up to date with immunizations as per current immunization guidelines. 3. Vedolizumab has orphan designations for the prevention and treatment of graft-versus-host disease (GVHD). However, its safety and efficacy in this context have not been established. 4. Co-administration of vedolizumab with tumor necrosis factor (TNF) blockers, such as adalimumab, certolizumab pegol, etanercept, golimumab, or infliximab, is not recommended due to the increased risk of infections resulting from additive immunosuppressive effects. Alternative therapies should be considered. 5. Vedolizumab decreases the efficacy of live virus vaccines, such as adenovirus types 4 and 7 oral vaccines, BCG vaccine, influenza virus vaccine (intranasal), measles-mumps-rubella vaccine, rotavirus oral vaccine, smallpox and mpox (vaccinia) vaccine, typhoid vaccine (live), varicella virus vaccine, yellow fever vaccine, and zoster vaccine (live). Live vaccines should generally be avoided during vedolizumab therapy unless the benefits outweigh the risks. 6. Vedolizumab may also reduce the effectiveness of recombinant zoster vaccines due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 7. Co-administration of vedolizumab with other immunosuppressive agents, such as baricitinib, upadacitinib, ozanimod, ponisemod, or etrasimod, may increase the risk of infections due to additive immunosuppressive effects. These combinations should be avoided or used with caution, and patients should be closely monitored. 8. Baricitinib is contraindicated in combination with other JAK inhibitors, biologic DMARDs, or potent immunosuppressive agents. 9. Vedolizumab may increase the immunosuppressive effects of CAR-T cell therapies, such as axicabtagene ciloleucel, brexucabtagene autoleucel, ciltacabtagene autoleucel, idecabtagene vicleucel, lisocabtagene maraleucel, and tisagenlecleucel, leading to an increased risk of infections. These combinations should be avoided or alternative therapies considered. 10. Vedolizumab may increase the toxicity of certain chemotherapeutic agents, such as ifosfamide, lomustine, mechlorethamine, oxaliplatin, and trastuzumab, due to additive immunosuppressive effects. Caution and close monitoring are recommended when these agents are co-administered. 11. Co-administration of vedolizumab with trastuzumab or trastuzumab deruxtecan may increase the incidence of neutropenia or febrile neutropenia, particularly when combined with myelosuppressive chemotherapy. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 12. Vedolizumab may increase the immunosuppressive effects of monoclonal antibodies, such as natalizumab, ofatumumab, and ublituximab, leading to an increased risk of infections. These combinations should be avoided or used with caution, and patients should be closely monitored. 13. When switching patients from therapies with prolonged immune effects, such as immunosuppressive agents or biologics, the duration and mechanism of action of the previous therapy should be considered to avoid unintended additive immunosuppressive effects. 14. Vedolizumab therapy requires careful consideration of the risks and benefits, particularly in patients with impaired immune systems or those receiving concomitant immunosuppressive therapies, due to the increased risk of serious infections.
